headword: {最高裁判所|さいこうさいばんしょ}
reading: さいこうさいばんしょ

definitions.gloss: Supreme Court; highest court of law
definitions.explanation: The highest judicial authority in a country. In Japan, the Supreme Court (located in Tokyo) serves as the court of last resort and has the power of judicial review over the constitutionality of laws.

examples.japanese: {最高裁判所|さいこうさいばんしょ}が{判決|はんけつ}を{出|だ}した。
examples.english: The Supreme Court issued a ruling.

examples.japanese: この{事件|じけん}は{最高裁判所|さいこうさいばんしょ}まで{争|あらそ}われた。
examples.english: This case was fought all the way to the Supreme Court.

examples.japanese: {最高裁判所|さいこうさいばんしょ}の{裁判官|さいばんかん}は{国民審査|こくみんしんさ}で{審査|しんさ}される。
examples.english: Supreme Court justices are reviewed through a national referendum.

notes: Compound of {最高|さいこう} (highest/supreme) + {裁判所|さいばんしょ} (court of law). Commonly abbreviated to {最高裁|さいこうさい} in news and conversation. Japan's court system has three levels: {簡易裁判所|かんいさいばんしょ} / {地方裁判所|ちほうさいばんしょ} (district courts), {高等裁判所|こうとうさいばんしょ} (high courts), and {最高裁判所|さいこうさいばんしょ} (Supreme Court). The Chief Justice ({長官|ちょうかん}) is appointed by the Emperor on the advice of the Cabinet.
